subject: Custody vs license — Order Form redlines and telemetry/training questions
messages:
From: Olivia Park <olivia.park@solismedia.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@solismedia.com
Date: Fri, 25 Jul 2025 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Custodial rights vs service license — Order Form draft

Marcus —

Thanks for the draft order form. Our legal team has inserted redlines and a few substantive asks we need to resolve before procurement can issue a PO. High-level items:

- Custody/assignment: we've flagged Section 6 (Output Ownership) because our product team expects exclusive control over downstream productization; they asked whether "assignment" language is intended. Our counsel prefers assignment for deliverables.
- Training/data use: your baseline MSA references a feedback license but doesn't explicitly forbid use for model retraining; please confirm whether Solis data or generated output could be used to improve internal models.
- Telemetry & evidence: we want audit evidence to show which model variant served requests and a basic token/latency log for troubleshooting.

I've attached the redlined OrderForm for your review (Solis_OrderForm_v1_redlines.docx). Can you route to legal and product and propose specific language we can live with?

Also copied procurement (legal@solismedia.com) — they need a path to PO issuance this month.

- Olivia Park
Sr. Counsel, Solis Media
-- attachment: Solis_OrderForm_v1_redlines.docx (docx)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@solismedia.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 25 Jul 2025 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Custodial rights vs service license — Order Form draft

Olivia —

Thanks for the redlines and the clear flags. Appreciate the procurement timeline; we'll move quickly. Quick answers up front:

1) Our preferred approach: we license output to customers (non-exclusive, perpetual) rather than accept assignment. That keeps our operational model consistent and avoids transfer of model IP. However, we can add a narrow carveout to allow your team to productize customer-provided outputs under a defined "deliverables" clause.

2) Training/data use: we do not automatically ingest customer content for general model retraining. We request an opt-in for retraining and will include an explicit training carveout in the Order Form if you require it. By default, feedback is used for service improvements only under an aggregated/anonymous signal unless explicitly contracted.

3) Telemetry/evidence: we can provide model-variant identifiers, request timestamps, and per-route token counts for a 12-month window as part of the Dedicated/Private package. For hosted contracts we can define an evidence-delivery cadence in the Order Form.

I've attached a tracked-changes proposal with suggested language that keeps license (not assignment) but adds a productization carveout and a narrow training opt-in: Redwood_proposed_edits.docx. Laura and Ben — can you review the edits and escalate any risky language? 

Proposed next steps:
- Redwood proposes edits (attached) 
- Solis counsel to confirm accept/counter 
- If accepted, Redwood legal to finalize and ops to confirm telemetry SLAs 

Goal: final Order Form + PO by 2025-07-31.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Sr. Solutions Counsel | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142
-- attachment: Redwood_proposed_edits.docx (docx)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 26 Jul 2025 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Custodial rights vs service license — Order Form draft

Marcus / Ben — forwarding Olivia's redlines and Marcus' proposal. My quick take (high level):

- Keep license approach. Assignment is a hard line; only accept if product/legal signoff and appropriate consideration. We risk precedent if we assign model outputs broadly.
- For the Deliverables carveout: define "Deliverables" narrowly (e.g., exported reports, generated assets delivered as files) and add export/derivative limitations to prevent wholesale retraining with PII or proprietary datasets.
- Training opt-in: explicit checkbox in Order Form + separate SOW for any retraining engagement. Include retention and deletion commitments.
- Feedback license: make explicit that feedback used for service-improvement is aggregated and non-identifying; separate clause if they want attribution/exclusive enhancements.
- Evidence: acceptable to provide model identifiers and token counts; deny full KV logs or raw prompt dumps by default. Consider a per-request redaction process for PII.

Suggested redlines are attached (RF_LegalRedlines_20250725.pdf). I recommend we propose the edited Order Form back to them with the Deliverables carveout and a training opt-in clause. Ben, we'll need an ops signal on SLA for the telemetry scope (12 months ok?).

Next steps (legal workflow):
1) Agree language internally
2) Send tracked-changes to Olivia (Marcus to send)
3) If Solis accepts, route to Legal Ops to prepare final MSA amendment or exhibit

Laura Bennett
Head of Commercial Legal | Redwood Inference
-- attachment: RF_LegalRedlines_20250725.pdf (pdf)

From: Olivia Park <olivia.park@solismedia.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@solismedia.com
Date: Sun, 27 Jul 2025 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Custodial rights vs service license — Order Form draft

Marcus, Laura —

Thanks for the quick turn. We reviewed Redwood_proposed_edits.docx and RF_LegalRedlines_20250725.pdf internally. A few follow-ups before we can accept: 

- Please send the Order Form with tracked changes visible (we couldn't see all comments in the PDF).
- On Deliverables: can you add a 6-month exclusivity window for any deliverables that our team marks as "beta product"? That is, Solis wants a short productization runway before Redwood can reuse or relicense those specific deliverables.
- Training opt-in: acceptable, but procurement wants a one-line statement in the PO that retraining will not occur without a separate SOW. Please confirm PO language sample.
- Telemetry: procurement will accept model-version and token counts, but they insist on a monthly CSV export that includes per-route totals (no raw prompts). Can Redwood confirm export format (CSV) and cadence?

If you can incorporate tracked changes and the PO one-line sample we can circulate to procurement for a PO issue. We're aiming to issue the PO by 2025-07-31 as well.

Regards,
Olivia Park
Sr. Counsel, Solis Media
